title: Creating Client Instructions and an Audit Trail
summary: Client guidance and project history replaced undocumented decisions and memory-dependent support.
principles: Documentation should help the client act and help the team reconstruct what happened.
looking_back: The maintenance requirement was the real constraint. Documentation that is too elaborate becomes another abandoned system, so the process had to fit the work already happening.
body: Clients lacked usable instructions, and the team had no durable history of project decisions, changes, or communication.
The system had to work for existing clients and remain practical enough for the team to maintain.
I introduced client-facing instructions alongside an audit trail documenting project history and decisions.
Clients gained clearer control of their sites, while the team gained organizational memory instead of relying on recollection.

perspectives.name: Julie
perspectives.text: The same documentation served two audiences: the client trying to act now and the team trying to understand later.

perspectives.name: Harbor
perspectives.text: An audit trail converts memory into continuity.
